Stated Claim / Post Context:
Man arrested for homicide two years after fatal robbery-related shooting in Nashville

A man has been arrested in connection to a fatal robbery-related shooting that happened two years ago in Nashville.

Actual Article Body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - A man has been arrested in connection to a fatal robbery-related shooting that happened two years ago in Nashville.

Metro Nashville Police said Monday that detectives arrested Akeemio Johnson, 32, earlier in the day. Johnson is suspected of shooting a man in the stomach in September 2024 during an attempted robbery.

Police said that during the 2024 incident, 37-year-old Francisco Ico Anx was outside a friend’s apartment when four people approached them, demanding their belongings.

“When Anx fought back, one of the suspects shot him in the stomach,” police said in a press release immediately after the incident. “They then shoved the second victim to the ground, threatening to kill him if he moved.”

Anx later died at Vanderbilt Medical Center.

Johnson will now be charged with criminal homicide for Anx’s death.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Russian street artist Slava Ptrk sums up four years abroad: ‘Unwanted There / Unwanted Here’ — Meduza

One of Russia’s best-known street artists, Slava Ptrk (Stanislav Komissarov), posted an Instagram photo of a new work exploring his own experience in exile. Komissarov left Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. Russian authorities designated him a “foreign agent.” The work, “Ne nuzhen tam / Ne nuzhen tut” (“Unwanted There / Unwanted Here”), is also called “Promezhutochnye itogi chetyrekh let emigratsii” (“Four Years in Exile: An Interim Assessment”). It consists of two signs styled like bus stop signs on opposite sides of the E22 highway near Yekaterinburg, his hometown. Ptrk has reimagined urban fixtures, including road signs, in previous works. In one of his best-known works, he turned a sewer grate across from the Kremlin into prison bars. In June, another sign appeared in Yekaterinburg beneath a road sign bearing the city’s name. It read “I Miss You.”
